rows.name: The Broken Robot Artist
steps: Educator plays 'The Broken Robot Artist' at the whiteboard: the class must make the robot draw a perfect square.
When a child says 'Draw a line', draw a messy squiggle; explain the instruction was too vague.
When a child says 'Draw a straight line across', draw it off the board; explain the robot was not told when to stop.
A child gives an exact command such as '30 centimeters to the right, then stop'; draw it.
Say 'Turn' spins the robot all the way round; the class asks for a 90-degree turn.
Restate: computers cannot guess what you mean.

levels.0: Board shows only squiggles; no instruction names a length or a turn.
levels.1: Instructions name a length but skip the 90-degree turn, so a corner is missing.
levels.2: Four equal sides with four 90-degree turns are named, and the board square closes.
levels.3: Instructions are shortened after a trial run, with a reason for each cut.

rows.name: Scratch: connect Green Flag to Move 50 Steps
steps: Write in the Tech Log: an input event trigger is the 'key' that unlocks the engine.

levels.0: No script is on the Scripts Area when the green flag is clicked.
levels.1: Green Flag and Move 50 are on screen but not joined, until a block is nudged for the pupil.
levels.2: Clicking the flag moves the sprite 50 steps, and a changed count changes the distance.
levels.3: Written prediction for 80 steps matches the distance seen on the Stage.

rows.name: Human Keyboard
steps: When the educator claps once (input), the whole room shouts 'Beep!' (output).

levels.2: Beep follows every clap and a jump follows every stomp, and the pupil names clap as input and beep as output.

rows.name: Number line from -5 to 20
steps: Lay a long strip of floor tape and mark 0.
Children write numbers on cards and place those below zero to the left.
Place cards from 0 to 20 to the right and read the line forwards and backwards.
Pick a start number and a rule such as +3; children walk and say the sequence.
Children order a jumbled set of number cards, including those below zero.

levels.0: Number cards are stacked unsorted beside the tape.
levels.1: Cards from 0 to 20 are in order but those below zero sit on the wrong side.
levels.2: Cards from -5 to 20 sit in order with zero marked, and the sequence is read forwards and backwards.
levels.3: Walking a fresh start number with a +3 rule, the sequence is called out.

rows.name: Line maze challenge
steps: Warm-up sketch activity with pencils on A4.
Introduce types of lines (wavy, zigzag, dotted, thick, thin) with board drawings or slides.
Line maze challenge: each pupil draws a path using 4 or more types of line.
Display on the wall as 'Our Line Worlds'.

levels.0: Maze path has fewer than two kinds of line.
levels.1: Maze path uses two or three kinds of line and one is shaky.
levels.2: Maze path uses four or more kinds of line, thick and thin, straight and curved.
levels.3: Wavy, zigzag and dotted lines are named aloud as the path is traced.

rows.name: Shape scavenger hunt and Shape Creature

Cut shapes from coloured paper.
Make a collage by arranging the cut-outs into an abstract 'Shape Creature'.
Show one Kandinsky image as background.
Display on the Shape Creatures Jungle board.
rows.materials: Magazines, child-safe scissors, glue, coloured paper.

levels.0: Creature uses only one kind of shape.
levels.1: Creature mixes shapes but none is organic.

levels.3: Creature's shapes are sorted aloud into geometric and organic groups.

Display as 'Our Class Quilt'.

levels.1: A repeat starts but breaks by the third unit.
levels.2: Pattern repeats cleanly across the whole grid row.
levels.3: Second row varies the colour rhythm while keeping the repeat.

rows.note: From the school's own curriculum document.

levels.0: Copy has no motif from the model.
levels.1: One motif is copied and its origin is not named.
levels.2: Warli or Ndebele motifs are copied and the place they come from is named.
levels.3: A motif's repeat or symmetry is pointed out on the copy.

Fill the inside with different pattern zones.
Add a background in crayon resist (watercolour wash).

levels.1: Silhouette has one pattern throughout.
levels.2: Silhouette has different line, shape and pattern zones.
levels.3: Wash background keeps the crayon patterns showing through.

rows.note: From the school's own curriculum document.

Make a Klee-inspired cityscape or Kusama-style polka-dot art.
Ask questions about the art and its style.
Display in the 'Inspired By…' corner.
rows.materials: Prints of the artists' work, paper, paints.

levels.0: Artist's lines or patterns are not mentioned.
levels.1: One line or pattern from the artist is noted.
levels.2: Lines and patterns used by Klee or Kusama are named from the print.
levels.3: Own artwork shows the same lines or dots, and a likeness is pointed out.

rows.note: From the school's own curriculum document.

levels.0: Plate has only the three primaries.
levels.1: Plate has one secondary, mixed with help.
levels.2: Plate shows orange, green and purple mixed from the primaries.
levels.3: Mixing recipe is told aloud for each secondary.

Display as a gallery by colour tone.
rows.materials: Paint trays, brushes, mood word chart.

levels.0: Painting mixes warm and cool colours at random.
levels.1: Painting is mostly warm or cool with a stray colour.
levels.2: Painting stays in warm or cool tones and the group is named.
levels.3: Title from the mood word chart suits the tones chosen.

rows.note: From the school's own curriculum document.

Uses at least two colours on the monster that suit the card's mood word.
Shows the monster to a partner when asked.

levels.0: Sky has flat colour with no stroke marks.
levels.1: Strokes appear in one part of the sky.
levels.2: Swirling strokes in layered colours cover the sky.
levels.3: Stroke and colour choices are linked to movement in the painting.
